hiclip.main_routing_conclusion: No confirmed consequential source mismatch identified in the targeted main-method, adaptor-pair encoding, control provenance and selected dependency-adoption checks. This is not whole-graph acceptance or exhaustive resource/algorithm review.

positive_preserved_distinctions.assessment: A and B are separately pre-adenylated stocks, both used in the first ligation. Permanent A ddC and removable B phosphate blocks remain distinct. The 50 percent productive-orientation expectation stays conditional on complete ligation, not an observed yield.

UV captures protein-RNA contact, whereas deblocked B mediates the later covalent arm-to-arm link. The graph contains an actual RNA-arm-B-RNA-arm material interface and retains nonhybrids; it is not merely a crosslink-site assay graph.

High/low RNase, second-ligation-minus and induction-minus library identities remain separate and carry their actual RT-primer assignments. UV-minus is confined to the smaller purification-condition test. High/low merging occurs explicitly downstream in data, not as an invented early material pool.

The physical 20/80 split, labeling of the 20 percent fraction and its recombination with the retained 80 percent are directly reported. This is a positive source-established return route, unlike an unreported analytical-aliquot fate inferred from topology alone.

Stringent urea denaturation and second capture are explicitly incorporated by the hiCLIP primary Methods, rather than silently imported solely from a background citation. Autoradiography supplies information used for membrane-region selection and RNA recovery.

RT orientation/truncation is qualified by the primary expectation; circularization/relinearization are cDNA steps explicitly reported in hiCLIP. The represented 100-300 nt interface is selected cDNA, not a falsely identical RNA insert-length claim. The included iCLIP explanation is applicable because the primary documents the same relevant operations.

B defines the paired-arm read boundary before separate arm mapping; pair identity remains retained. Nonhybrid start-site protein-RNA contacts remain distinct from model-assisted duplex calls. Same-mRNA mapping is not promoted into proof of pairing within a single physical RNA molecule.

Literal ligation-volume ambiguities, stored B-A branch reentry and incomplete candidate/tie/extension implementation stay explicit. Random-arm controls are data controls; unique-rRNA benchmarking is a separate supporting subset, not a claimed universal production filter.

hiclip.source_reading_boundary: Registered table2 contains a large historical result table. No requirement to reread every historical coordinate row was imposed to describe the general method; original binary figures and exact numerical execution were not independently validated.
hiclip.source_adoption_boundary: Primary Methods directly support stringent purification, library circularization/relinearization and the described RNAhybrid call boundary. Missing ancestral protocols/code need not block these qualified known interfaces; their absence does prevent full historical execution/code reproduction claims.

correction_assessment.assessment: Adds ligation-preparatory 5-prime phosphate to the end-repair function/product and carries it into A-tailing/ligation interfaces. Table 2 identifies End Repair Mix phosphate addition and its 5-prime-OH control substrate. The record explicitly calls this manufacturer-described kit chemistry, not a separately measured Fuchs end-chemistry experiment.

Adds the guide alternative of 10 microliters resuspension buffer with 50 microliters ds cDNA before 40 microliters mix when the optional in-line control is absent. It stays an explicit guide recipe rather than an established Fuchs handling choice.

Adds avoid-same-index pooling, 10 microliter normalization/pooling aliquots, 2-24 libraries and 20-240 microliter pool size with guide attribution. The primary only establishes pooled PE50 sequencing after delegated TruSeq RNA v2 preparation. Exact Fuchs pool ratios/index mapping remain unresolved; no unqualified primary adoption of these guide settings was found.

Also adds optional size/purity QC sampling and an inspection operation. Bioanalyzer versus Fragment Analyzer are alternatives, with their actual 1 microliter library and RSB qualifications. The approximately 260 bp expectation remains single-read-only, not a PE50 acceptance threshold, and size/purity observations do not become an invented adaptive loading controller.

fields./operations/10/information_effect: Produces library quantity data and separates analytical material from retained production stock. The size/purity aliquot yields a separate inspection readout; analytical qPCR products and inspected aliquots do not enter production pooling.
fields./operations/11/information_effect: Produces size/purity observations associated with the sampled library. The inspection aliquot remains outside the production path; no source-described decision rule uses this readout to govern sequencing or normalization.
fields./operations/12/input_bindings/1/basis: In the optional manufacturer QC route, withdraw 10 μL from retained production stock for guide normalization, then pool selected normalized-library aliquots. Analytical qPCR and inspection portions do not enter the pool.
fields./modules/3/boundary_rationale: Separates optional manufacturer analytical qPCR quantity data and size/purity aliquot inspection from retained indexed production stock, pooling and sequencing. Platform aliquots are alternatives; neither analytical material nor its products return to production. Only reported yield-based guide normalization uses quantity data.
fields./states/27/description: Optional guide Bioanalyzer route: a physical 1 μL aliquot of one resuspended indexed library, retaining its sample/index association for size/purity inspection. Distinct from the qPCR portion and the remaining production stock; no return to production is reported.
fields./states/28/description: Alternative guide Fragment Analyzer route: a physical 1 μL aliquot of one resuspended indexed library diluted with 1 μL RSB, retaining sample/index association. Distinct from the qPCR portion and remaining production stock; no return to production is reported.

qualification_watchpoint.assessment: New aliquot states correctly say no return to production is reported. Operation/module prose instead categorically says analytical material or products do not enter/return to production. Source sampling and original-stock transfers support the drawn separate paths; they do not independently document every eventual aliquot fate or an absolute prohibition on reuse. Because the route is optional, guide-qualified and its retained-stock handoff is expressly inferred, this is a narrower wording watchpoint, not a finding that Fuchs executed the route or that returning material occurred. Keep topology absence distinct from experimentally established negative fate.
